hook: $40 an hour. One mistake. You keep $15.66
hook_say_short: Forty bucks an hour. Sounds fine, right?
hook_say: Here is a $40 hourly rate that looks like $76,800 a year. It has one mistake: it counts every hour as paid. See if you spot it before the reveal.

rows.label: Rate on the price list
rows.say: Here's how most people do the math. $40 an hour
rows.tts: Here's how most people do the math. Forty an hour

rows.label: Hours worked (48 wks x 40)
rows.tts: times about nineteen hundred and twenty hours a year.

rows.label: Looks like a year of
rows.why: $40 times 1,920 hours. The mistake: it assumes clients pay for every hour.
rows.tts: Seventy-six thousand, eight hundred. Not bad.

rows.label: Hours clients pay for (60%)
rows.say: The mistake: clients don't pay for every hour. Here, it's about six in ten.
rows.why: Quoting, driving and admin are work nobody pays for. The example bills 60% of hours.
rows.tts: The mistake? Clients don't pay for every hour. Quoting, driving, emails... here it's about six hours in ten.

rows.label: Kept per hour worked
rows.say: Take out tax and costs, and you keep $15.66 an hour. Fifteen.
rows.why: $46,080 of revenue, less $6,000 of costs and a 25% tax set-aside, leaves $30,060 over 1,920 hours worked.
rows.tts: [sighs] Take out tax and costs, and you keep fifteen sixty-six an hour. Fifteen.

fix.label: Hourly rate for $60,000 take-home
fix.why: $74.65 rounded up for a rate card: $86,000 of revenue needed over 1,152 paid hours.
fix.tts: Want sixty grand in your pocket? Charge seventy-five.

post.short_title: This $40 rate has one mistake. You keep $15.66 #Shorts
post.reel_caption:
$40 an hour over 1,920 hours looks like $76,800. Spot the mistake? Clients pay for only 1,152 of those hours, so after tax and costs you keep $15.66 for every hour you work. To take home $60,000, charge $75. Example numbers from the Hourly Rate Quick Calculator.
